# Vendor meetings

Recurring vendor meetings are working sessions with a record, not relationship
theater, and their discipline is what makes the quarterly evidence trail complete.

Preparation is asymmetric on purpose: our side arrives with the ticket-derived
agenda — the open items, the aging commitments, the response-window arithmetic since
last meeting — circulated to the vendor beforehand, so the meeting starts at the
evidence instead of reconstructing it.

The meeting runs the agenda in commitment order: existing commitments are verified
or re-dated first, because a meeting that opens with new business quietly rolls old
commitments forward forever. New items enter the record as dated, verifiable
statements before the meeting ends, in wording both sides heard.

The record lands in the ticket archive the same day, linked from every ticket the
meeting touched, with commitments extracted into the same structure the escalation
policy measures. A meeting that produced no record did not happen, and its verbal
commitments do not exist.

Relationship tone is professional and durable: the record never carries frustration,
attributions of bad faith, or private remarks, because every meeting record is
written as if the vendor will one day read it in a renewal negotiation — which, in
evidence form, they will.

## Cancellation discipline

A recurring meeting with nothing on the ticket-derived agenda is cancelled ahead of
time with the empty agenda attached, and two consecutive empty agendas trigger a
cadence review. Meetings held to hold them erode the record's meaning: an archive
full of contentless meeting notes teaches readers to skip meeting notes.
